name: Rootskin — The Geneware Heritage Reveal Challenge
creator: Popularized by geneware artist Chiamaka Nwofor-Baig via pirate neural feed channel; later co-opted by HelixCorp's consumer geneware division
description: Participants used cosmetic geneware to temporarily express phenotypic traits drawn from every strand of their genetic ancestry simultaneously — skin tone shifts, hair texture variations, eye pigmentation changes, bone structure softening — wearing the full visible spectrum of their heritage on their body for 72 hours. The challenge began as an intimate act of self-archaeology on Shelf pirate feeds before exploding across all tiers when Tier 3 and 4 participants began posting their experiences to licensed neural feed channels.
medium: physical geneware expression, documented via neural feed visual broadcast
cultural_impact: Rootskin briefly collapsed the usual Meridian social performance of identity — in a city where 'exotic' had no meaning, it made visible what Ubiquitous Diaspora had blended invisible, forcing conversations about whether heritage was something you carried or something you performed. It also exposed the vast cost gap between black-market Shelf geneware and licensed Tier 4 versions, since cheap gene-expression patches caused skin scarring in several hundred documented cases.
controversy: The Clearskin movement condemned Rootskin as 'retrogressive identity theater.' More seriously, HelixCorp's rapid licensing of a premium 'Rootskin Kit' at Φ2,400 was widely denounced as extraction — the company had monitored pirate feeds, reverse-engineered the Shelf geneware formula, patented a stabilized version, and began marketing it to Tier 3-4 consumers within six months of the trend's peak. The original Shelf participants received nothing. A class grievance petition gathered 400,000 neural signatures before being dismissed.
story_hooks: A runner on the Shelf discovers that the cheap Rootskin patch they used three years ago left a dormant geneware trigger in their dermal layer — someone with the right signal can activate it remotely

The original Shelf artist who created Rootskin resurfaces after two years of silence, claiming HelixCorp's patent is built on stolen genetic data harvested from Shelf residents without consent, and they have the receipts

A Tier 5 Spire socialite who participated in the trend via the luxury kit finds themselves obsessed with tracing the ancestry the geneware revealed — and what they find doesn't match what their family has always claimed
